transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Ms. Williams, thank you for coming back in to see me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't stay long. I have to pick up my kids soon.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I wanted to talk to you about the discharge papers you were given on Tuesday. There was a mistake regarding the follow-up clinic we listed for your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What kind of mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The referral was sent to a facility that isn't in-network with your insurance provider. Because of that, they won't be able to see you for your post-op checkup. I'm sorry for any confusion this caused, but we were incredibly short-staffed in the discharge office that morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I didn't know that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It basically means the insurance won't cover the visit there, so we have to find a different provider who actually accepts your plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just need to make sure I'm healing right. I can't afford to be sick. My kids need me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We just need to get the paperwork sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just worried. Everything is already so hard.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, the main thing is that the current appointment is essentially void.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Do you follow what I'm saying so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good. We just need to pivot to a new clinic.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will it be far? I only have one car and I'm working two jobs right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We'll look for something closer.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope it's soon. I've been feeling a bit tired.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That can be normal for recovery. As for the next step, I'll have my coordinator look into some options.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Probably in a few days. We'll try to find a place that works.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I really can't miss any more work.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We'll get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll just have the office reach out to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will they call or email?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure, but they'll get in touch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Is there anything else you need right now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. I just want to go home to my children.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That makes sense.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't want this to be a problem with my insurance.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It shouldn't be, we're just fixing the referral.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll let you get going then.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Have a good afternoon.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and adjusts pacing to the patient's distress without interrupting or using rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn, lay language was used, and comprehension was checked once ('Do you follow what I'm saying so far?').

A.justification: A direct apology was offered, but it was immediately diluted by an excuse regarding being 'incredibly short-staffed'.

R.justification: The resident used generic validation ('I understand') multiple times but never named a specific emotion back to the patient.

T.justification: A next step was provided with a vague timeline ('a few days'), but there was no named patient role or mention of prevention.
